title: Lessons 1 to 5 Practice Exam
lessons: 4. How you'll work with Claude on your desktop

questions.prompt: What does 'Constitutional AI' refer to in the context of Claude?
options: A legal framework governments use to regulate AI companies
An approach where Claude is trained with guiding principles to avoid harmful or discriminatory outputs and align with human values
A feature that lets users upload their own company constitution for Claude to follow
A setting that restricts Claude to answering only from approved company data
questions.explanation: Claude is guided by principles that help it avoid toxic or discriminatory outputs and illegal or unethical help, and behave as a safe and beneficial assistant.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Claude's context window is correct per the course?
options: It is limited to about 32K tokens on every plan
It is unlimited on all plans
It can ingest 200K+ tokens (about 500 pages), with up to 1M tokens on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise using supported models
1M tokens is available only on the Free plan
questions.explanation: 200K+ tokens is roughly 500 pages of text; up to 1M tokens is available on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise with supported models.

questions.prompt: In the 'thinking partner vs search box' exercise, what is the deciding factor for which one a request needs?
options: How long the request is
Whether the topic is technical or non-technical
Whether the request contains a question mark
Whether the answer depends on the person's own situation, draft or judgment
questions.explanation: Search handles standalone facts. A thinking partner is needed when personal context shapes the answer. The topic itself is not the deciding factor.

questions.prompt: Which Claude offering brings Claude directly into Slack, where you can tag it in threads?
options: Claude Design
Claude Tag
Claude Code
Claude for Microsoft 365
questions.explanation: Claude Tag is the Slack integration. Claude Design builds interactive prototypes, Claude Code is the agentic coding tool, Claude for Microsoft 365 covers Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook.

questions.prompt: The course's prompt framework has three parts. Which option lists them correctly?
options: Setting the stage, defining the task, specifying rules
Delegation, description, discernment
Role, length, temperature
Context, command, conclusion
questions.explanation: Set the stage (role, objective, context), define the task (the action), specify rules (style, tone, format, examples). Delegation/description/discernment belong to the 4D AI Fluency framework.

questions.prompt: Which model does the course recommend as the default for everyday users, and which for the most complex tasks?
options: Opus for everyday use, Sonnet for complex tasks
Sonnet for everyday use, Opus for complex tasks
Sonnet for both
Opus for both
questions.explanation: Sonnet balances capability and cost and is the recommended default. Opus is the largest model with hybrid reasoning, for the most complex tasks.

questions.prompt: What happens when you change the model using the model selector in an existing chat?
options: It results in a new chat
The same chat continues with all history intact
Your memory is cleared
Your uploaded files are deleted from your account
questions.explanation: Changing the model results in a new chat.

questions.prompt: What is the default state of Memory?
options: Off on all plans
On by default on every plan including Team and Enterprise
On by default on Free, Pro and Max; off by default on Team and Enterprise until an organization Owner allows it
On only for Enterprise plans
questions.explanation: On by default on Free, Pro and Max. On Team and Enterprise it is off by default and can be turned on in Settings > Memory once an organization Owner allows it.

questions.prompt: Claude's response to your email request is too generic. According to the course, what is the best fix?
options: Switch to a different language
Make the prompt shorter
Ask the same prompt again until it changes
Add details about your audience, role and constraints
questions.explanation: Generic output usually means the prompt lacked context about your specific situation.

questions.prompt: In the 4D Framework for AI Fluency, which competency covers thoughtfully and critically evaluating AI outputs, processes and behaviors?
options: Delegation
Description
Discernment
Diligence
questions.explanation: Discernment = evaluating quality, accuracy and appropriateness. Delegation = what goes to humans vs AI. Description = communicating with AI. Diligence = responsible, ethical use.

questions.prompt: Rio tests whether Claude is suitable for his quarterly analysis. What approach did he follow?
options: Trusted Claude's first answer because it sounded confident
Ran the analysis only on brand-new data so there was no bias
Asked Claude to grade its own work
Used past data he had already analyzed, had Claude reproduce it, compared results, refined, and tested again
questions.explanation: This is the delegation-diligence loop: test on a case where you know the right answer, evaluate gaps, refine, re-test. If Claude cannot match known results, the task may not be one to delegate.

questions.prompt: Claude gave a confident-sounding fact that turned out to be wrong. What does the course recommend?
options: Verify key facts independently, ask for sources or confidence level, and enable web search to ground responses
Assume it will not happen again in the same chat
Ask Claude to repeat the answer more confidently
Only use Claude for creative tasks
questions.explanation: Claude can occasionally produce plausible but incorrect information, especially for specific facts or niche topics. For high-stakes work, verify, ask for citations, use web search.

questions.prompt: You want a Monday-morning briefing assembled from your messages, notes and calendar, ready before you start work. Which shape of work and which feature fits best?
options: Turn-by-turn work in Chat
Building software in the Code tab
Handing work off in Cowork using a scheduled task
Creating a Project with instructions only
questions.explanation: Multi-step work spanning your tools that runs on a schedule is a hand-off, which lives in Cowork (scheduled tasks).

questions.prompt: What is the concrete difference between Chat and Cowork regarding files?
options: Chat can never read uploaded files
Cowork can only create text files
There is no difference
Cowork can access a local folder and save finished work back there, while Chat hands finished files back as downloads
questions.explanation: Cowork gets local folder access and saves finished work into it. Chat can read what you upload but returns files as downloads.

questions.prompt: Per the course, where do scheduled tasks run?
options: They run remotely even if your computer is asleep, except tasks needing local files, which run locally only while the app is open
Always locally, only while the app is open
Only in the Code tab
Only on Enterprise plans, always remotely
questions.explanation: Scheduled tasks generally run remotely (computer asleep or app closed is fine). A task that needs files on your computer runs locally, only while the app is open.

questions.prompt: You're brainstorming ideas and each answer determines what you ask next. Which shape of work is this?
options: Handing work off in Cowork
Working turn by turn in Chat
Building software in the Code tab
A scheduled task
questions.explanation: When the answer changes what you ask next, you are working turn by turn, which is Chat.

questions.prompt: What do project instructions do?
options: They apply only to the first chat created in the project
They replace your user preferences completely
They apply to every chat in the project and work alongside your user preferences
They are visible only to teammates, not to Claude
questions.explanation: Project instructions guide tone, expertise level and response style in every chat in the project, alongside user preferences.

questions.prompt: What happens when a project's knowledge approaches the context window limit?
options: Claude refuses new questions
Claude deletes the oldest files
Claude automatically enables RAG, retrieving only relevant parts and expanding capacity by up to 10x
The project is automatically archived
questions.explanation: Projects scale using Retrieval Augmented Generation: Claude searches project files and pulls in only what is relevant, expanding capacity up to 10x.

questions.prompt: A teammate has 'Can view' permission on your shared project. What can they do?
options: See contents, access knowledge and chat, but not make changes
Edit instructions and manage members
Delete the project
Only see the project name
questions.explanation: Can view = read-only plus discussion rights. Can edit can modify instructions, update knowledge and manage members. The Owner controls everything.

questions.prompt: You want to share a document with Claude for one conversation in a project without adding it to the project's knowledge base. What should you do?
options: Add it to the knowledge base, then delete it later
Put it in the project description
Create a new project for it
Upload it directly in the conversation; it stays separate from project knowledge
questions.explanation: Files uploaded during a chat stay separate from project knowledge. The project description is not seen by Claude directly.
